title: DID YOU BRING US OUT TO KILL US?

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"But the people were thirsty for water there, and they grumbled against Moses.
They said, 'Why did you bring us up out of Egypt to make us and our children and
livestock die of thirst?'" - Ex 17:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice the first line: "the people were thirsty."

Scripture does not dismiss their thirst. It names it. This was not imagined
suffering or spiritual weakness. They had children and animals and no water in a
desert. The need was real and urgent.

That matters, because we can read these chapters as though Israel were simply
whiners. They were not. They were frightened people in genuine danger who
handled it badly.

And here is the accusation again: "to make us and our children die." They assign
murderous intent to the God who split a sea for them.

This is what unaddressed fear does over time. It does not stay as fear. It
curdles into suspicion about God's motives. First we doubt His timing, then His
methods, then His heart.

The remedy Scripture offers is not to suppress the fear but to speak it to God.
"Cast all your anxiety on him because he cares for you" (1 Pet 5:7). Notice the
reason given: because He cares. The antidote to suspicion about God's heart is
learning what His heart is actually like.

Look at the cross before you decide what God intends toward you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Has fear started to make you suspicious of God's motives?
2. What does the cross say about how God feels toward you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, when fear tells me lies about Your heart, remind me of the cross. I bring
You my anxiety because I know You care. Amen.
